messages:
marta: Heads-up — our nightly latency bench (ci-nightly / v0.12.3) showed steady mem growth on the prealloc worker pool. RSS goes from ~7.2G to ~12.6G over 45m on a steady 120 qps replay. Not a hard OOM yet but looks bad.

ashwin: Oof. Is this new to 0.12.3 vs 0.12.2? Any kernel logs or oom-kill happening?

marta: We compared against a 0.12.2 baseline — 0.12.2 stayed stable. No oom-kill. dmesg/ journal is clean. Heap growth visible in `ps`/`top`. I captured a pmap and a quick /proc/PID/smaps snapshot.

marta: ```
$ pmap -x 12345 | tail -n 5
12345:   total kB   12896320   12896320   197312

$ sudo awk '/^Rss:|^AnonHugePages:|^VmRSS:/ {print $0}' /proc/12345/status
VmRSS: 12963200 kB
AnonHugePages: 0 kB

# smaps shows a lot of anonymous dirty pages creeping up in a few mmapped regions.
```

ashwin: Can you enable mallctl / jemalloc stats print for that process? MALLOC_CONF=stats_print:true on startup or use je_malloc_conf? That will show arena fragmentation and retained extents.

james: Also please run `jeprof` or get a jemalloc heap profile if possible. If we're not on jemalloc (glibc/tcmalloc), collect heapshot or /proc/PID/smaps over time. We should check retained vs active pages.

marta: Restarting one worker with `MALLOC_CONF=stats_print:true` now. I also added `--mem-profile=/tmp/mem.prof` flag to the runtime (the binary supports it). Will attach after it runs ~15m.

olivia: If it helps, run `LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libjemalloc.so.2` too on a dev machine to compare allocator behavior. Sometimes glibc mmap arenas lead to unreturned pages.

ryan: Quick ask: can someone run `perf` for a few minutes to see if there's busy-loop allocation hotspots? Command I usually run: `perf record -g -p $PID -- sleep 60; perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded; flamegraph.pl out.folded > perf.svg`

marta: Started the perf run. Also saving `/proc/12345/smaps` every 60s to s3: `while true; do cp /proc/12345/smaps /tmp/smaps.$(date +%s); aws s3 cp /tmp/smaps.$(date +%s) s3://redwood-debug/mem-leak/ ; sleep 60; done &`

infra-bot: heapdump saved to s3://redwood-debug/mem-leak/heap.1769804390.heap (size 1.2G) — triggered by `/admin/collect-heap 12345`

ashwin: Nice. Once we have the jemalloc dump, look at `allocated` vs `active` vs `mapped`. If `active - allocated` is huge, it's internal fragmentation. If `mapped - active` is large, it's extents not returned to OS.

james: If it is fragmentation, two mitigation experiments: 1) set `MALLOC_CONF=\"background_thread:true,dirty_decay_ms:10000,muzzy_decay_ms:10000\"` to encourage return; 2) try `jemalloc` opt that enables `tcache` smaller or `purge` hooks. We can test locally before pushing.

marta: Heap profile attached (uploaded to s3). Quick grep shows repeated allocations in `gpt_tokenizer::tokenize` and `kv_cache::reserve` hotspots. But the main oddity is lots of mmapped anonymous ranges with lazy allocations.

olivia: Could be our prealloc pool policy combined with address-sanitizer-like behavior? Are we leaking arena objects or holding onto big vector capacities? Check sites that call `Vec::reserve` in a hot path — maybe capacity not trimmed.

ryan: I can instrument a small replay that toggles growth flags: runtime with `--prealloc-pool=0` vs `--prealloc-pool=1` to see if prealloc is the cause. Worth a quick A/B.

marta: Did that. prealloc disabled -> RSS stays ~7.3G stable. prealloc enabled -> drift to 12G. Reproducible on dev. So the pool is a likely suspect.

ashwin: Ok great repro. Next steps: 1) add guardrails to the pool so it trims to target after N idle seconds; 2) instrument pool to log total reserved bytes and counts; 3) consider switching pool allocator to use MADV_FREE on returned extents (if OS supports) so RSS drops.

james: I put a draft PR to add a `--pool-trim-interval` flag and a background trim task. @marta can you test the branch? PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345

marta: Testing now on the repro cluster. Early signal: RSS stops growing and slowly trims back by ~30% over 2m. Looks promising. Will run longer 2h run tomorrow.

olivia: If that looks good, we can ship the opt as a hotfix to nightly and gate dedicated pools behind it. Also add observability: expose `pool_reserved_bytes` metric in console so ops can detect this earlier.

marta: Agreed. I've left notes in the PR and added a small unit test that simulates repetitive reserve/return churn.

infra-bot: nightly job `ci-nightly/mem-regress` triggered for PR 2345 — results will be posted in #eng-runtime after run completes.

ryan: Thanks team. If anything regresses or we still see slow growth after trim, we'll run a deeper jemalloc config sweep. For now let's keep the pool off for Dedicated customers until we verify. :+1:

marta: Thanks all — will post the 2h run summary tomorrow with graphs (RSS, malloc stats, smaps diffs).
